effort: Read an opponent’s rhythm change and use the brief moment when movement becomes available.
brief: Consolidate Class 8’s decision load by limiting direction choices and emphasizing timing. E1 starts with both people already moving so the athlete reads a change of pace, not another stationary go cue. Low unilateral ankle return, short scissor impulse, controlled reburst, catch-to-release reversal and an offensive timing window supply distinct support jobs.
anchor_protocol: Coach and athlete move slowly forward on parallel paths, athlete about half a step behind, both within a 2–6 m work strip. During a ≤4 s bout the coach makes one clear acceleration then one clear easing/stopping action, with no direction change. Athlete matches the pace change without closing the marked longitudinal gap, stops within 2 m beyond the strip. Four bouts. If response history is unknown, make the pace change broad and slow; do not increase duration. Record whether acceleration and braking were read separately.
quality_marker: E1: correct response to both pace changes, preserved gap and a controlled stop. Record the coach’s sequence and speed description; no claim of speed improvement from a different drill or different cue rhythm.
layout: Use parallel 10 m lanes with verified ≥2 m lateral separation. E1 total athlete travel ≤4 m per bout plus ≤2 m stopping. E4 starts at 1 m, builds for 2 m, floats for 1 m, rebursts for 1 m and stops by 7 m. E5 coach and athlete face each other about 2 m apart in an isolated, verified catch zone; use a ball light enough for soft underhand delivery and controlled fast return, not a hard chest-height projectile. E6 uses protected parallel attacker/defender paths and a marked 2 m athlete gate route; there is no body contact.
progression: Previous: Class 8 prescribed two-direction decisions with twelve mixed landings. Current: timing without directional branching, six low-amplitude single-leg pogo contacts plus two controlled scissor-bound contacts, and only six primary set rounds. This is an intentional reduction of supporting demand, not a response to invented fatigue. Hold actual strength loads and cue pace unless executed reps/RIR and recovery show readiness; the next progression would narrow a timing window, not simultaneously add contacts.
audit: Pace matching, planned reburst and an offensive opportunity window have different decision/control jobs. Six low ankle contacts and two low bounds are recorded separately from earlier larger hops. Catch-to-return uses soft delivery and a controlled hip yield; it is rapid force reversal, not ordinary catching counted as strength. One challenging set in each primary slot maintains the six-exercise structure while reducing total demand. Next class addresses route choice with clear boundaries.

explosive.name: Moving Opponent Tempo Match
explosive.job: Main rhythm task: detect acceleration and easing from an already-moving opponent while preserving a useful gap.
explosive.execution: Begin at a slow shared pace, respond to one pace increase and one stop/easing, travel ≤4 m, stop in ≤2 m. Rest 75 s between bouts and 90 s before E2. Widen the pace contrast if either event is missed.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Single-Leg Pogo in Place
explosive.job: Practice small repeated ankle return on one support leg for an unpredictable next step.
explosive.execution: Three low hops in place on one foot, stop after the third; repeat opposite after 60 s. Rest 60 s before E3. Soft knee, tall torso; reduce amplitude for heel slap or lateral drift.

explosive.name: Straight-Leg Bounds — low amplitude
explosive.job: Create a quick alternating hip-driven impulse with little knee lift or flight height, complementing ankle-only pogos.
explosive.execution: Take two short forward straight-leg-style bounds with softly unlocked knees, alternating feet; low height and no reaching for distance. End controlled. Rest 90 s before E4. Shorten stride for hamstring tension or braking on a locked leg.

explosive.name: Build–Float–Reburst Run
explosive.dose: 1 × 3 repetitions of 2 m build + 1 m float + 1 m reburst
explosive.job: Physically rehearse changing force output while already moving without adding a directional choice.
explosive.execution: Use marked segments at controlled speed, then stop within 2 m. Float is reduced drive, not walking or an abrupt brake. Rest 75 s between reps and 60 s before E5. Reduce overall speed if the reburst causes overstriding.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Soft Medicine-Ball Catch-to-Scoop Return
explosive.job: Accept a small incoming load through the hips/trunk and reverse it promptly into a forward release, supporting tempo changes in force expression.
explosive.execution: Coach sends a soft low underhand pass; receive with two hands near the waist, yield slightly through hips/knees and immediately return underhand without a jump. No hard throw or deep squat. Rest 30 s between releases and 60 s before E6. Reduce load/delivery for collapsing posture or slow arm-only returns.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

explosive.name: Bait-and-Go Timing Window
explosive.job: Read when a defender’s weight commitment creates time to leave, introducing an offensive timing problem.
explosive.execution: Coach guards a corresponding gate on a separate parallel path, then makes one visible weight commitment away from it. Athlete may make a small nontravelling shoulder feint, but bursts 2 m only when the window opens; stop within 2 m. Rest 75 s between bouts, 90 s before strength. Make the opening longer for premature or missed departures.
explosive.source: Proposed drill/exact execution; no library ID claimed.

stabilization.name: Short-Foot Drill — both feet supported
stabilization.job: Low-fatigue foot control after unilateral ankle contacts.
stabilization.execution: Keep both feet supported and work one target foot at a time: maintain heel and metatarsal contact while gently raising the arch, with long toes. Relax 5 s between holds; use seated support instead if toes curl. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

stabilization.name: Heel-Dig Bridge Hold — light bilateral
stabilization.job: Easy heel-driven posterior-chain tension before a reduced-volume strength block.
stabilization.execution: On a comfortable floor surface, heels down and knees bent; lift hips only to a stacked trunk and gently pull heels toward the hips without moving them. Keep easy and breathe; lower height for cramp or back extension. Rest 30 s between sides/holds and 30 s before the next exercise. Stay at RPE 3–4/10, at least five clean reps or ample hold time in reserve.

primary.name: Goblet Squat
primary.job: Retain knee/hip force with one quality set during timing consolidation.
primary.execution: Hold one dumbbell at the chest; sit between the hips with whole-foot pressure and rise smoothly. Use an owned depth; reduce load/range for heel lift or trunk collapse. Rest 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Reverse Lunge — dumbbells
primary.job: Single-leg acceptance and return from the ready stance without adding another compound round.
primary.execution: Step one foot backward, lower under control, then use the front leg to return to standing. Keep the front heel down; shorten the step/load for wobble or push-off from the rear toes. Rest 90 s between sides; 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Hip Thrust — sandbag
primary.job: Hip extension for the reburst after a period of reduced drive.
primary.execution: Support upper back on a stable bench, secure the sandbag across the hip crease, drive through both feet and finish with ribs stacked. No lumbar arch; reduce load for pelvic loss. If bench fit fails, use a floor glute bridge instead, same dose, recording the shorter range. Rest 120 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 60 s before working sets.

primary.name: Partner Manual-Resistance Hamstring Curl
primary.job: Controlled knee-flexor force during alternating running contacts.
primary.execution: Lie prone on a comfortable floor surface; coach applies smooth resistance above the heel while the athlete bends and straightens the knee through an owned range. Keep hips down; no sudden pushes. Match resistance to 2–3 RIR, not a contest. If prone support/contact is unsuitable, use Seated Band Hamstring Curl instead, same sets/reps per side: sit on a stable bench, secure a light band at the heel with a coach holding steady forward tension, then pull the heel beneath the bench without moving the thigh. Qualify band/bench fit; no sudden release. This replaces only this slot and preserves totals. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise — supported standing, dumbbell
primary.job: Maintain ankle push capacity with unchanged support and heel range.
primary.execution: Stand on flat floor with a nearly straight knee and light hand support; raise the heel, pause briefly and lower for 2 seconds. No bounce or ankle roll. Reduce load when heel height declines. Rest 60 s between sides; 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 3/side easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.

primary.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise — bilateral, bent-knee
primary.job: Maintain bent-knee force for the braking response to an easing opponent.
primary.execution: Use a stable bench, knees near right angles, secure dumbbells on distal thighs above knees. Lower heels for 2 seconds to the floor, pause, then rise. Reduce load for bouncing or shortened range. Rest 60 s before the next exercise.

preparation.dose: 1 × 5 bilateral easy; 30 s between sides where applicable, then 45 s before working sets.
